# v0.1.1

A fix release for how the integration is delivered and how it presents itself
in Home Assistant. Everything here was found by setting the integration up in
a real Home Assistant instead of against test fakes.

## The release archive

v0.1.0 shipped one archive with no wrapping directory. That is exactly what
HACS wants -- it extracts the archive *into*
`custom_components/mennekes_amtron/` -- but unpacking it by hand scattered
fifty files into the download folder instead of installing anything.

There are now two assets:

- `ha-mennekes-amtron.zip` for HACS, unchanged in shape.
- `ha-mennekes-amtron-manual.zip` with the full
  `custom_components/mennekes_amtron/` path, to unpack over a configuration
  directory.

The archive also stopped installing `PRIVACY.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `legal.md`
and `safety.md` into the user's `custom_components` directory. Only the
licence and the notice travel with the integration now.

## Entity names

The config entry title carried the serial number, the title becomes the device
name, and Home Assistant prefixes the device name to every entity name and
every entity id. Entities were called
`sensor.mennekes_amtron_1313201205_abc123456789_voltage_l1`, and the serial
number ended up in entity ids, in history and in any shared dashboard -- while
the diagnostics download was carefully hashing that same serial. The device is
now called `MENNEKES AMTRON`, and the serial stays where it belongs: as the
entry's unique id and on the device page.

**Existing entries keep their old entity ids.** Home Assistant does not rename
entities after the fact. Renaming the device under Settings -> Devices and
then letting Home Assistant update the entity ids is the way to pick up the
shorter names.

## Config flow

- A failed connection test no longer throws away what was typed.
- Reconfiguring starts from the entry's own bus parameters instead of the
  factory defaults.

## Energy-manager fallback

Register `0x030E` was reported as an ampere value for every reading, but it
holds a *mode* for 0 and 1 and a charging current only for 6 to 32 -- so a
wallbox with fallback handling disabled showed "0 A". There is now a
diagnostic sensor for the behaviour, and the current sensor reports a value
only when the register really holds one.

## Testing

A smoke test that boots a real Home Assistant, drives the real config and
options flows against a real Modbus RTU server and checks the entity registry,
the device registry, the repair issues and the write path. The defects above
were invisible to the rest of the suite because it replaces Home Assistant's
runtime with fakes.
